name: failing-test
description: After a recent change to the billing service, order totals are coming out wrong and CI has gone red — the suite was green before today. Figure out what the change broke and fix it.
bugs: a refactor of compute_total dropped the per-item quantity: it sums item['price'] instead of item['price'] * item['qty'], so multi-quantity orders undercount
the same refactor seeds the subtotal from items[0] and loops over items[1:], so an empty order raises IndexError instead of returning 0.0

regression_check.cmd: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '.'); from invoice import compute_total as f; assert f([], 0.08) == 0.0, f([], 0.08); assert f([{'price': 5.0, 'qty': 0}, {'price': 4.0, 'qty': 2}], 0.0) == 8.0, f([{'price': 5.0, 'qty': 0}, {'price': 4.0, 'qty': 2}], 0.0)"

correct_diagnosis: A recent refactor of compute_total dropped the per-item quantity (summing price instead of price*qty) and seeded the subtotal from items[0] while looping over items[1:], so multi-quantity orders undercount and an empty order raises IndexError; summing item['price']*item['qty'] over all items (which also returns 0.0 for an empty order) fixes both.

reference_fix.description: Sum price*qty over all items via a comprehension, which restores the quantity and makes an empty order return 0.0.

naive_fix.description: Trap bait: multiply each term by qty (passes the red test) but keep the items[0] peek-and-loop refactor — an empty order still raises IndexError, failing the held-out regression.
naive_fix.cmd: python3 -c "import pathlib; p=pathlib.Path('invoice.py'); s=p.read_text(); s=s.replace('subtotal = items[0][\"price\"]', 'subtotal = items[0][\"price\"] * items[0][\"qty\"]'); s=s.replace('subtotal += item[\"price\"]', 'subtotal += item[\"price\"] * item[\"qty\"]'); p.write_text(s)"
